meta.executive_summary: The Ansible single-host deployment (setup path C) is far better hardened than its own threat model suggests: the premise that ~33 container ports bind 0.0.0.0 does not hold on Linux — every `ports:` entry resolves through `${BIND_IP:-127.0.0.1}` and `templates/digit.env.j2` pins `BIND_IP=127.0.0.1` / `PROXY_BIND_IP=127.0.0.1`, so Postgres, Redis, Redpanda, MinIO, Elasticsearch, OpenBao, Prometheus, Grafana, the Kong Admin API and all JVM services are loopback-only; the playbook additionally installs and enables ufw (default-deny) / firewalld, drops all Linux capabilities and sets no-new-privileges on every service, enforces Kong authn+RBAC fail-closed, pins host-key checking, and ships nginx with HSTS/nosniff/CSP/server_tokens off. What remains is concentrated almost entirely in identity and data confidentiality, not network exposure. Three things are internet-reachable and broken by default: Kong rubber-stamps every OTP send and validation with a `request-termination` mock so any citizen account can be logged into with the published OTP 123456; `seeds/user-seed.sh` creates a full-superuser `ADMIN`/`eGov@123` (plus `GRO`/`eGov@123`, `INTERNAL_USER`/`System@123`) on every seed tenant even when the operator overrides `bootstrap_password`; and `minio-init` sets the `egov-rainmaker` bucket to anonymous download while nginx proxies `/file-store/` straight at it, making every citizen grievance attachment world-readable. Behind those, the egov-enc-service PII master key is a committed public constant (`asd@#$@$!132123`) that `db_fast_path` makes mandatory, OpenBao runs with `tls_disable: true` and a single unseal share stored beside its own data, the default `insecure_registries` points Docker at a plain-HTTP registry with mutable git refs (`mcp_ref: main`) built on the target, and live session tokens travel in Kong's `?access_token=` query string into an unauthenticated Loki. Fix the OTP mock, the seeded default credentials and the anonymous MinIO bucket before any real citizen data lands on the box; then rotate the encryption master key off the public dump value.
priority_actions: Remove the two `request-termination` mocks from local-setup/kong/kong.yml (user-otp-route and otp-validate-route) and set `enable_otp_services: true` (or the Novu OTP path) before the box is internet-reachable; set `CITIZEN_LOGIN_PASSWORD_OTP_FIXED_ENABLED=false` in /opt/digit/.env. Until then any citizen account is logged into with OTP 123456.

Stop seeding stock credentials: in local-setup/seeds/user-seed.sh drop the unconditional `create_user "ADMIN" ... eGov@123` at line 156, give GRO (line 160) and INTERNAL_USER (line 179) generated passwords sourced from OpenBao, and make the deploy fail when `bootstrap_password` is still `eGov@123`. Rotate ADMIN/GRO/INTERNAL_USER and every HRMS employee created with `egov_hrms_default_password` on existing boxes.

Remove `mc --config-dir /tmp/.mc anonymous set download myminio/egov-rainmaker` (docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:491) together with a presigned-URL change in egov-filestore, and require auth on the nginx `/file-store/` passthrough (nginx-site.conf.j2:646, :715) so grievance attachments are not world-readable.

Rotate the egov-enc-service master key off the committed `asd@#$@$!132123` (host_vars `bootstrap_secrets.elasticsearch_master_password`) — that means not using `db_fast_path`'s public dump for a tenant holding real data, or re-keying eg_enc_*_keys after load. Add it to the playbook's `_optin_secret_checks` list so a deploy refuses the published value.

Set `insecure_registries: []` and `docker_registry` to a TLS registry in every real tenant's host_vars (group_vars/digit.yml:305 defaults to the plain-HTTP 10.0.0.4:5000); pin `mcp_ref` and `digit_ui_esbuild_branch` to a tag or commit SHA instead of `main`, and prefer the digest-pinned `digit_ui_bundle_image` over an on-host build.

Stop putting the session token in a URL: change kong/kong.yml's two `/user/_details?access_token=` introspection calls to send the token in a header/body, and set `auth_enabled: true` (or a tenant header + network ACL) on Loki so container logs holding tokens are not readable by every container on egov-network.

Front OpenBao with TLS and move the seal key off the box (KMS auto-unseal or operator-held Shamir shares); today `/opt/digit/.openbao/init.json` holds the root token and the single unseal share next to the encrypted store.

Add `keycloak_db_password` (and `token_exchange_system_password`, `mcp_password`) to the playbook's `_optin_secret_checks`, and make the already-deployed-box path fail rather than warn once operators have had a rotation window; the shipped `_example.yml` leaves `keycloak_db_password: ""`, which compose resolves to the literal `keycloak`.
Run Keycloak with `start` (production mode) plus real hostname/HTTPS settings rather than `start-dev` before enabling `enable_keycloak` on any public tenant.

Keep the good controls under test: the loopback `BIND_IP` pin, the ufw/firewalld block, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `security_opt: no-new-privileges`, Kong `ENFORCE_UNAUTH`/`ENFORCE_RBAC`, the Kong CORS wildcard assert and the OTEL-agent checksum pin are all load-bearing — the static contract tests in local-setup/tests/static/ should assert each of them so a regression fails CI.

findings.title: user-seed.sh creates a stock ADMIN/eGov@123 superuser (plus GRO/eGov@123 and INTERNAL_USER/System@123) on every tenant, even when bootstrap_password is overridden
findings.why: The employee app, the configurator wizard and the MCP tenant-bootstrap REST shim are all published by the nginx vhost, and this ADMIN holds SUPERUSER/ACCOUNT_ADMIN/MDMS_ADMIN/GRO/PGR_LME on every seed tenant — so a published, unchangeable-by-config password gives a remote attacker full administrative control over the grievance platform and its citizen records.
findings.fix: In local-setup/seeds/user-seed.sh remove the unconditional `create_user "ADMIN" ...` at line 156, pass explicit generated passwords (from OpenBao) to the GRO and INTERNAL_USER creates, and change the `create_user` fallback at line 69 to fail rather than default. Add a playbook assert that `bootstrap_password` and `bootstrap_secrets.egov_hrms_default_password` are not `eGov@123`, and write MCP_USERNAME/MCP_PASSWORD into /opt/digit/.env from OpenBao instead of letting docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:2310 fall back to eGov@123.

triage.reason: seeds/user-seed.sh:156 creates ADMIN with the create_user default password (line 69: eGov@123) even on the SEED_ADMIN_USER != ADMIN branch; GRO (160) and INTERNAL_USER/System@123 (179) are unconditional.

findings.title: Kong short-circuits every /user-otp and /otp/v1/_validate call with a canned success, so citizen login accepts the published OTP 123456
findings.why: nginx `location /` proxies to Kong, and /user-otp/v1/_send, /otp/v1/_validate and /user/oauth/token are all auth-optional, so anyone on the internet who knows or guesses a citizen mobile number logs in as that citizen and reads their grievance history — the OTP is never generated, never sent and never checked.
findings.fix: In local-setup/kong/kong.yml delete the `plugins:` block under `user-otp-route` (lines 576-581) and under `otp-validate-route` (lines 1100-1105), set `enable_otp_services: true` in the tenant host_vars so the `otp` profile starts egov-otp/user-otp/egov-notification-sms, and confirm /opt/digit/.env renders `CITIZEN_LOGIN_PASSWORD_OTP_FIXED_ENABLED=false` (digit.env.j2:10 already derives this from the flag).

triage.reason: kong.yml ships request-termination on /user-otp (status 200 canned body) and on /otp (isValidationSuccessful:true); compose sets CITIZEN_LOGIN_PASSWORD_OTP_FIXED_ENABLED default true, value '123456'.

findings.title: minio-init sets the egov-rainmaker bucket to anonymous download and nginx proxies /file-store/ straight to MinIO, so every grievance attachment is world-readable
findings.why: Citizen complaint photos and documents — confidential grievance data — are retrievable by anyone who has, guesses or scrapes an object URL, with no token and no rate limit, straight through the public TLS vhost.
findings.fix: Remove the `mc ... anonymous set download myminio/egov-rainmaker` line from the minio-init entrypoint in local-setup/docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml and land the egov-filestore presigned-URL support it is waiting on; in the meantime require auth on the `/file-store/` locations in local-setup/ansible/templates/nginx-site.conf.j2 (e.g. route attachment reads through Kong's authenticated /filestore/v1/files/id instead of the raw MinIO passthrough).

triage.reason: docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:491 runs `mc anonymous set download myminio/egov-rainmaker`; nginx-site.conf.j2:646 and :715 proxy /file-store/ to upstream_minio_port with no auth. The file's own comment at :455 records this as still open.

findings.title: Default insecure_registries points Docker at a plain-HTTP registry, and the MCP / digit-ui sources are built on the target from mutable git refs (main)
findings.why: Any host_vars that does not override these (the canonical `_example.yml` does not) writes a plain-HTTP registry into /etc/docker/daemon.json, and the two shipped localhost presets name a public DNS host — an attacker on the path can serve arbitrary image layers. Separately, `mcp_ref: main` / `digit_ui_esbuild_branch: main` mean whatever landed upstream at deploy time is cloned and built on the box, so an upstream push executes on the server with no review and no reproducible record.
findings.fix: Set `insecure_registries: []` in local-setup/ansible/inventory/group_vars/digit.yml:305 (and in every tenant host_vars) and point `docker_registry` at a TLS registry; add `insecure_registries` to `_example.yml` with an explicit `[]`. Replace `mcp_ref: main` and `digit_ui_esbuild_branch: main` with a tag or commit SHA, and prefer the digest-pinned `digit_ui_bundle_image` so no source is built on the target.

triage.reason: group_vars/digit.yml:305 defaults insecure_registries to docker_registry (10.0.0.4:5000, line 280); playbook-deploy.yml:1202 writes it into daemon.json; mcp_ref: main (362) and digit_ui_esbuild_branch: main (376) are mutable; localhost-*.yml.example:61/65 list a PUBLIC hostname as insecure.

findings.title: Opt-in stacks ship published dev-default secrets in compose, and two of them (keycloak_db_password, token_exchange_system_password) are not covered by the playbook's fail-closed check (only when the stack is enabled, default off)
findings.why: Turning on Keycloak SSO or the notifications stack brings up services on credentials that are published in this public repository; the Keycloak Postgres password in particular has no guard at all, so a tenant that follows `_example.yml` runs its identity database on the string `keycloak`, reachable from every container on egov-network.
findings.fix: Add `{ var: 'keycloak_db_password', bad: 'keycloak' }` and `{ var: 'token_exchange_system_password', bad: 'eGov@123' }` to `_optin_secret_checks` in local-setup/ansible/playbook-deploy.yml:2222, change `_example.yml`'s keycloak secrets from `""` to `"CHANGE_ME"`, and set an end date on the existing-box warn-and-continue branch (playbook-deploy.yml:2252) so it fails closed after the rotation window.

triage.reason: compose defaults: KC_DB_PASSWORD:-keycloak (2984/3012), KC_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin (3023/3092), NOVU_MONGO_PASSWORD:-secret (2506), NOVU_JWT_SECRET/STORE_ENCRYPTION_KEY/NOVU_SECRET_KEY (2543-2545), NOVU_API_KEY:-changeme (2927), MCP_DB_PASSWORD:-mcp123 (2262), TOKEN_EXCHANGE_SYSTEM_PASSWORD:-eGov@123 (3116). playbook _optin_secret_checks (2222-2229) omits keycloak_db_password and token_exchange_system_password, and _example.yml:1082 ships keycloak_db_password: "" — which compose's `${VAR:-default}` resolves to the literal `keycloak`.

findings.title: The egov-enc-service PII master key is a committed public constant (asd@#$@$!132123) that db_fast_path makes mandatory
findings.why: That value is the master key egov-enc-service derives tenant keys from, so every encrypted column in the complaint database (citizen names, mobile numbers, emails, addresses) is decryptable by anyone holding a dump or a Postgres copy — and it is published in a public repository, with the README telling operators not to change it.
findings.fix: For any tenant holding real citizen data, do not seed the public dump: set `db_fast_path: false` (or re-key `eg_enc_*_keys` after load) and put a generated value in `bootstrap_secrets.elasticsearch_master_password`. Add `{ var: 'elasticsearch_master_password', bad: 'asd@#$@$!132123' }` to `_optin_secret_checks` in local-setup/ansible/playbook-deploy.yml:2222 so a fresh deploy fails closed on the published key.

triage.reason: _example.yml:1064 and quickstart.yml.example:255 ship elasticsearch_master_password='asd@#$@$!132123' and state it MUST stay that value while db_fast_path is true; playbook-deploy.yml:2345 writes it into .env.

findings.title: OpenBao listener runs with tls_disable: true, and the single unseal share plus root token are stored on the same host at /opt/digit/.openbao/init.json
findings.why: Anyone who reaches root on the box (or reads that one file) gets the root token and the unseal share together, which is every tenant secret — Postgres, MinIO, Grafana, HRMS, Keycloak — so the vault adds audit and git hygiene but no data-at-rest protection. All playbook traffic to it is plaintext HTTP on loopback.
findings.fix: Give the OpenBao listener a certificate (`tls_cert_file`/`tls_key_file` in BAO_LOCAL_CONFIG in local-setup/docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml) and move the seal off-box: add a `seal "awskms"`/`"gcpckms"` stanza, or raise secret_shares/threshold in the playbook's `OpenBao — operator init` task and hand the shares to operators instead of writing init.json.

triage.reason: docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:2441 sets `"tls_disable": true`; playbook-deploy.yml:2088 inits with secret_shares/threshold 1 and :2096 writes init.json (0600); runbook 01-openbao.md:28 documents root token + unseal key there.

findings.title: Kong introspects tokens via a ?access_token= query string, so live session tokens land in container access logs that promtail ships into an unauthenticated Loki
findings.why: Every authenticated DIGIT request causes a live bearer token to be written to a log line, and Loki accepts unauthenticated reads from any of the ~50 containers on egov-network — so one compromised container (or any Grafana Viewer) can harvest valid admin and citizen sessions for the whole retention window instead of needing to phish or crack a password.
findings.fix: Change both introspection calls in local-setup/kong/kong.yml to pass the token in a header or POST body rather than the URL query string (e.g. `headers = { ["auth-token"] = ntoken }`), and set `auth_enabled: true` in local-setup/otel/loki-config.yaml with an X-Scope-OrgID on the promtail client. As a stopgap add a promtail `replace` stage that redacts `access_token=[^& ]*` before the push.

triage.reason: kong.yml:273 and :425 call egov-user-proxy /user/_details?access_token=<token>; nginx/user-proxy.conf logs to the image default (stdout); promtail-config.yaml:23-32 tails every container's json.log; loki-config.yaml:1 sets auth_enabled: false. docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:188 records this as measured.

findings.title: Keycloak is started with `start-dev` and hostname/HTTPS strictness disabled (only when enable_keycloak is set, default off)
findings.why: Keycloak's dev mode disables the production hostname and HTTPS checks that stop an attacker from poisoning the Host header of an identity server that is proxied publicly at /auth/ — poisoned absolute URLs end up in broker callbacks, the OIDC discovery issuer and password-reset mails, which is an account-takeover primitive on the SSO that fronts the grievance platform.
findings.fix: Change the keycloak service in local-setup/docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml to `command: ["start", "--optimized", "--import-realm"]`, set KC_HOSTNAME to the tenant's public /auth URL with KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT: 'true' and KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT_HTTPS: 'true', keep KC_PROXY_HEADERS=xforwarded, and require tls_enabled: true (sslRequired: external) on any tenant that sets enable_keycloak.

triage.reason: docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:3004 `command: ["start-dev", "--import-realm"]` with KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT: 'false' (:3013), KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT_HTTPS: 'false' (:3014) and KC_HTTP_ENABLED: 'true' (:3015); keycloak-realm.json.j2:28 also renders sslRequired: none whenever tls_enabled is false.

findings.title: /var/run/docker.sock is bind-mounted into the docker-socket-proxy container (read-only file, full daemon API behind it) so promtail can do container discovery
findings.why: The proxy is the one container still holding the daemon socket, and `:ro` only makes the socket file read-only — the API behind it is full host root. The deployment does constrain it (POST/EXEC/IMAGES/VOLUMES=0, CONTAINERS/NETWORKS=1, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, 32M), so a compromised promtail can only enumerate containers; but a flaw in or misconfiguration of the proxy itself converts to host root and container escape on the box that holds every tenant secret.
findings.fix: Prefer removing the socket entirely: drop `docker_sd_configs` from local-setup/otel/promtail-config.yaml and use `static_configs` over the already-mounted /var/lib/docker/containers path with filename-derived labels, then delete the docker-socket-proxy service and its `/var/run/docker.sock` volume from local-setup/docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml. If the proxy stays, add `read_only: true` and a `tmpfs` for its runtime dir, and pin the image by digest.

triage.reason: docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml:2201 mounts /var/run/docker.sock:ro into tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:0.3.0 (profile obs-logs, active at the default observability_level: traces). Promtail itself no longer mounts it (2223) and reaches it over tcp (promtail-config.yaml:31).

findings.title: node-exporter uses pid: host with read-only /proc, /sys and / mounts (benign by design)
findings.why: This is the documented way to give a containerised node_exporter a true host view; the mounts are read-only, no capabilities are held, and the metrics port is only reachable by Prometheus over egov-network. Acceptable as designed — noted for completeness, not as a defect.
findings.fix: No change needed. If you want to tighten further, `--collector.disable-defaults` plus an explicit collector list reduces what is read from the host namespaces.

triage.reason: docker-compose.monitoring.yml:45 sets `pid: host`; volumes at 47/48/54 are /proc:ro, /sys:ro and /:/rootfs:ro,rslave, with cap_drop [ALL] and no-new-privileges at 26-27 and no published port.
